AIM Workshop “Pólya-Schur-Lax Problems: Hyperbolicity and Stability

record.original_question: Given degree-n real homogeneous polynomials p and q in k variables, is the Fischer-Fock inner product ⟨p,q⟩ bounded below by Cap(p)·Cap(q)·n!/k^n?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k,n\ge 1$ be integers. The Fischer–Fock space $\mathcal F_k$ is the Hilbert space of holomorphic functions on $\mathbb C^k$ equipped with the inner product
$$\langle f,g\rangle_{\mathcal F_k}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N^k}\alpha!\,a(\alpha)\,\overline{b(\alpha)},$$
where $f(z)=\sum_\alpha a(\alpha)z^\alpha$ and $g(z)=\sum_\alpha b(\alpha)z^\alpha$ are the Taylor expansions of $f$ and $g$, and $\alpha!=\alpha_1!\cdots\alpha_k!$.

For a polynomial $p\in\mathbb R[z_1,\dots,z_k]$ with nonnegative coefficients, define its capacity by
$$\mathrm{Cap}(p)=\inf_{x_1,\dots,x_k>0}\frac{p(x_1,\dots,x_k)}{x_1\cdots x_k\cdots}\quad\text{i.e.,}\quad \mathrm{Cap}(p)=\inf_{x\in\mathbb R_{>0}^k}\frac{p(x)}{x_1 x_2\cdots x_k}^{?}$$
(more precisely, for a homogeneous polynomial of degree $n$ in $k$ variables with nonnegative coefficients, $\mathrm{Cap}(p):=\inf\{p(x_1,\dots,x_k)/(x_1\cdots x_k)^{n/k}:x_i>0\}$ when $k\mid n$, and the natural extension via $\inf p(x)$ subject to $\prod x_i=1$ otherwise).

Question: For any two real homogeneous polynomials $p,q\in\mathbb R[z_1,\dots,z_k]$ of degree $n$ with nonnegative coefficients, does the inequality
$$\langle p,q\rangle_{\mathcal F_k}\;\ge\;\mathrm{Cap}(p)\,\mathrm{Cap}(q)\,\frac{n!}{k^{\,n}}$$
hold?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located the problem as Gurvits's Problem 3 from the AIM workshop on Pólya–Schur–Lax problems, but did not return a paper resolving the Fischer–Fock capacity inequality in either direction. Subsequent works (e.g., "Capacity Lower Bounds via Productization", 2020; "Counting Matchings via Capacity Preserving Operators", 2021) develop capacity-based techniques but do not appear to settle this specific bilinear inequality. Status appears unverified.
